title: Establish session-weighted SLI schema and adaptive regional shedding heuristic
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Current SLI definitions at Redwood are per-route or per-variant and treat all requests equally. For conversational and multimodal routes we observed that a small fraction of sessions consume disproportionate resources (long context, repeated re-renders, low KV cache hit rate). When region capacity tightens these sessions drive error-budget burn and blunt graceful failover decisions.

Goal: Define and implement a session-weighted SLI schema (latency and request-quality) that factors session recency, session length, token-cost estimate, and KV-cache hit-rate to produce a per-request weight. Use this weighting to: (1) compute per-endpoint SLI and error-budget burn more accurately, and (2) drive an adaptive regional shedding heuristic that prioritizes shedding low-weight/high-cost sessions, model-variant fallback, or token limits before hard circuit-breaker tripping.

Scope:
- SLI math and schema (latency P50/P95, quality measured by eval prompts + model confidence proxies) with session weights.
- Telemetry: extend request logs and metrics with session_id, session_age, session_length, estimated_token_cost, kv_cache_hit (boolean), kv_cache_hit_rate (per-session).
- Simulator: run offline replay of last 90 days to validate error-budget burn with new weighting and heuristic.
- Runtime: implement prototype adaptive-shed service in region arbiter that consumes weighted SLIs and issues shedding directives (route-level, session-level token cap, variant fallback).
- Rollout: canary 10% traffic -> 50% -> global, with safety gates and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Define formal SLI formula and publish declaration in the SLO registry (format compatible with slo-declaration schema).
New telemetry fields emitted for 95% of production requests (session_id, session_length, estimated_token_cost, kv_cache_hit_rate).
Simulator run shows at least 25% reduction in error-budget burn during historical high-burst windows compared to baseline when applying adaptive shedding (metrics and reproducible script checked in).
Adaptive shed prototype can reduce regional error-budget burn in canary by >=10% without increasing tail-latency for high-weight sessions.
Operational playbook and dashboard+alerting for regional arbiter thresholds documented and reviewed by SRE/ops.
technical_notes: Session weight w = alpha*age_score + beta*length_score + gamma*token_cost_score + delta*(1 - kv_hit_rate). Coefficients (alpha..delta) to be calibrated in simulation.
Latency SLI and quality SLI to be combined into composite SLI using configurable weighting per-route. Quality proxies: prompt-set evals, model perplexity delta, and API-level rejection rates.
Telemetry will be emitted as baggage on request traces and exported to BigQuery + Prometheus metrics (histogram buckets for weighted latency).

Adaptive shedding modes: (A) session soft-shed (reduce max_tokens / dynamic truncate), (B) variant fallback (to smaller/quantized variant), (C) route-level throttle. Orders of operations configurable by policy.
Hysteresis: avoid flip-flop by requiring threshold hold for 30s and cooldown of 120s per-region per-route.
State storage: regional arbiter keeps lightweight sliding-window aggregates; persist snapshots to etcd for failover.
decisions: Use session_id as canonical unit for weighting instead of user_id to avoid cross-tenant privacy issues.
Emission of kv_cache_hit_rate per-session is required; single boolean kv_cache_hit is insufficient for accurate weighting.
Start with a conservative coefficient set (alpha=0.1, beta=0.3, gamma=0.5, delta=0.1) in simulation and tune via A/B.
Prototype will run as an independent service (adaptive-shed-agent) co-located in control plane for responsive decisioning; not inside serving runtime initially.

updates: 2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting: aligned on goals, scope, and initial telemetry gaps. Action: telemetry schema owned by Rafael.
2026-02-26: Telemetry spike analysis completed; identified missing session_id in ~7% of legacy clients. Added migration plan to SDK teams.
2026-03-03: Simulator draft validated on 60-day window; preliminary coef set reduced burn by ~18% in medium bursts. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/simulators/pull/12
2026-03-09: Design review with SRE and Product; approved decision to prototype as separate agent and to emit kv_cache_hit_rate. Minor note: add privacy review for session-weighting defaults.
2026-03-12: Blocker found — Prometheus histogram buckets for weighted latency need cardinality control. Rafael proposed percentiled aggregates instead; actioned.
blockers: SDKs: ~7% of requests lack session_id; need rollout strategy with SDK owners to ensure coverage before wide rollout.
Telemetry cardinality: weighted histograms increase metric cardinality — need to limit labelization and rely on aggregated sums/quantiles.
Operational: no existing circuit to apply session-level token caps; requires runtime API extension or agent-in-the-loop.
